brief.headline: Global AI Rout Drags Down Tech Stocks; Indian Markets Eye Resilience at Open
brief.summary: Global markets reeled from a severe tech and AI sector selloff, pushing the S&P 500 into correction territory and the Nasdaq 100 into its worst week since March 2020 following Anthropic's debut and Nvidia scrutiny. Domestically, Indian equities showed resilience with strong banking outperformance and FII inflows lifting the Nifty toward the 26,200 resistance zone. Meanwhile, hospital and corporate stocks remained in focus amid strong earnings optimism and regulatory updates.

takeaways.text: Global tech and AI stocks suffered a massive correction, with the Nasdaq 100 sinking 5.6% and Nvidia tumbling amid regulatory and accounting probes.
Indian banking stocks led a robust monthly rally, pushing Nifty Bank to a record intraday high of 64,485, supported by strong PSU and private participation.
Hospital stocks including Max Healthcare, Apollo Hospitals, and Fortis rallied up to 14% on strong earnings visibility and growth optimism.
Crude oil prices are projected to normalize to USD 70 per barrel by the end of 2027 due to expected market surpluses.
An Anthropic researcher claimed an AI-assisted solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, marking a notable milestone for mathematical AI capabilities.

sections.india: Indian equities demonstrated strong momentum last week, with the Nifty surging 2.61% toward resistance at 25,950–26,200 backed by robust FII inflows. Banking shares spearheaded the advance as Nifty Bank touched a record intraday high of 64,485, while healthcare names like Max Healthcare and Apollo Hospitals extended sharp gains. Corporate developments remained active with Adani Energy bagging a 2,500 MW renewable supply project and Ashok Leyland planning a new plant in Singur.
sections.world: Global financial markets suffered a severe risk-off shock led by a brutal selloff in US technology and AI-related shares. The S&P 500 entered correction territory down 3.70%, and the Nasdaq plummeted 5.28% in its worst week since the Covid-19 crisis following Anthropic's public market debut. Commodities also saw broad-based declines, with Brent crude down 2.21% to USD 89.95 and gold logging its worst week since March.
sections.tech: The technology sector confronted a severe reality check as regulatory investigations intensified around Nvidia, spanning California criminal probes and SEC accounting inquiries. Despite the market turmoil, Anthropic's Claude-powered research made headlines as a staffer claimed a breakthrough solution to the Riemann hypothesis. Meanwhile, Apple advanced its autonomous AI agent strategy to rival OpenAI and Meta.

Geopolitical tensions, particularly between the US and Iran, are likely to influence oil supply dynamics.
